metadata.title: Interest Media.
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Vanakkam (Tamil), one word — fresh for this channel (Namaste, Kumusta, Sawubona, Hej, Merhaba and Jambo are spent on the six prior reels). IN-FOR-BEAR LAW applies in its Yatra form this time, at the human's explicit request: Bella is the STAND-IN VOICE on Yatra's own @Yatra channel, so (a) the greeting slot carries the NARRATOR's name per the law ('[hello], Liam' → 'Vanakkam, Bella'), (b) B00's first breath says the voice out loud — 'this is Bella, in for Yatra' — and (c) the outro signs off the same way. The footer chip stays @Yatra, exactly as @NikBearBrown stays the chip on a Liam reel. Voice: Kokoro af_bella (free, local).
metadata.color_semantics: Fidelity claude palette. ONE terracotta #D97757 event per beat, and it always marks THE INTEREST SIDE of the shift — the new sort key, the stranger's post that travelled, the question that replaced the old one. The accent carries the thesis (what you care about beat who you know) rather than decorating the frame. Attribution and provenance stay muted ink, never accent.
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00 (cold open, ask lands ANSWERED), B06 (ask micro-beat of the one ask→result pair, resolved by B07), B10 (verdict artifact), B11 (handoff), B12 (outro). Every other beat illustrates with a purpose-built Itm* scene. ATTRIBUTION (hard, per the human): the 'interest media' framing is Gary Vaynerchuk's and is credited by name on screen at B02 and again at B09; it is PARAPHRASED THROUGHOUT and never quoted — ItmSource has no `quote` prop, only `claimParaphrase`, so no words can be put in his mouth. NO INVENTED NUMBERS: not one figure, percentage, count or date appears anywhere in this reel — every scene type in InterestMedia.tsx is numeral-free by construction (see FACTCHECK.md).

beats.narration_text: Hello, this is Bella, in for Yatra, reading Yatra's notes this week. They open on something Gary Vaynerchuk said — and it changes the question. Not who follows you. What people are actually interested in.

show.event: Cream page, serif greeting 'Vanakkam, Bella' above the composer — the app greets the narrator, the footer chip stays @Yatra
The ask types itself in
Terracotta send arms — the ONE accent
Three result lines stagger in; the third names the new sort key — the ask lands ANSWERED

props.command: Gary Vaynerchuk argues social media has become interest media. Explain the shift from follower-based feeds to interest-based feeds — and what it changes for someone making content. Credit him, paraphrase him, and do not invent any statistics.
output: the old sort key: who you know — your follows, your contacts
the new sort key: what you care about — watched, paused, searched
so the gate moved: a post can now travel before an audience exists

beats.narration_text: Here's the whole idea in one breath. Social media stopped running on who you know. It runs on what you're interested in. And that changes what a post has to do to travel.

show.event: Claim one sets in serif with a growing ink rule beside it: 'It stopped running on who you know.'
Claim two sets beneath, and this one lands in TERRACOTTA — 'It runs on what you're interested in.'
Claim three sets in ink: 'So a post has a different job.'
Closer lands beneath the stack: 'The feed changed its sort key.'

data.slideMeta: The whole idea, before any detail

claims.label: It stopped running on who you know.
It runs on what you're interested in.
So a post has a different job.

data.closer: The feed changed its sort key.

beats.narration_text: The idea is Gary Vaynerchuk's. His point was blunt: social media as we knew it is basically dead. Not gone — transformed. What we're in now is closer to interest media. Social media asks who you know. Interest media asks what you care about.

show.event: Attribution card opens: the name Gary Vaynerchuk, in muted ink — provenance never takes the accent
The paraphrase band sets beneath it, stamped PARAPHRASED — NOT A QUOTE
The word SOCIAL rules through on 'not gone — transformed'
INTEREST types in above it in TERRACOTTA — the rename lands
Question one sets under the struck word: 'Who do you know?'
Question two sets under the new word: 'What do you care about?'

data.claimParaphrase: Social media, as we knew it, is basically dead — not gone, transformed. What we are in now is closer to interest media.
data.note: One idea, credited. The rest of this is what it looks like from inside a feed.

beats.act: YOUR OWN FEED — the worked example
beats.narration_text: Test it on your own feed. When did it last show you your cousin, or your old college roommate? Probably not recently. You're seeing strangers instead — because the algorithm noticed what you watched, what you paused on, what you searched for.

show.event: Left column heads PEOPLE YOU FOLLOW and fills with three plain cards — your cousin, your college roommate, a friend from work
On 'probably not recently' the left column DIMS as a block — dimmed, never below the 40% legibility floor
Right column heads WHAT YOU'RE ACTUALLY SEEING and fills with cards marked 'not followed'
Three signal chips light along the bottom rail in order as they are spoken: WATCHED · PAUSED ON · SEARCHED
A terracotta wire runs from the signal rail up into the right column — the ONE accent, and it points at the cause

data.slideMeta: The same feed, two ways of reading it
data.leftFoot: when did the feed last show you one of these?
data.note: The feed is not reading your contact list. It is reading your attention.

beats.narration_text: This didn't happen by accident. There's too much posted every single day for your network of friends and family to surface the best of it. The network stopped being able to sort.

show.event: A small ring of network nodes draws — friends and family, labelled YOUR NETWORK
Post marks begin falling into the frame from above, sparse at first
The fall thickens into a field that fills the whole stage — no count is shown or implied, only density
The network ring is overwhelmed and its sorting rule fades out
A terracotta band lands across the field: 'more than a network can sort'

data.slideMeta: Why the old sort key gave out
data.title: Too much, every single day
data.verdictBand: more than a network can sort
data.note: No number here on purpose — the point is the density, not a figure.

beats.narration_text: So the platforms changed the question. They stopped asking who do you know. They started asking what do you actually care about.

show.event: The sorter draws as a machine: posts enter on the left, a keyed slot in the middle, the feed leaves on the right
The old key seats in the slot, labelled 'who do you know?' — posts route by follow lines
On 'they stopped asking' the old key lifts out and greys
The new key drops into the slot in TERRACOTTA, labelled 'what do you care about?'
The routing re-runs through the new key and the output feed re-orders — the mechanism performs the sentence

data.note: Nobody announced this. The key just changed.

beats.narration_text: Here's the part that matters for a marketer. I wanted the two models drawn side by side.

show.event: Composer returns with the generation prompt already arriving
Terracotta send arms
Running indicator reads 'drawing both models…' — the result is the next beat

props.command: Draw the two models side by side: the follower model, where reach is gated behind an audience you have to build first, and the interest model, where one post can travel on match alone. No numbers — just the gate and the match.

beats.narration_text: In the old model you needed thousands of followers before anyone saw your work. Followers were the gate. Now a single well-made post can reach people who've never heard of your brand — because it matches what they already care about.

show.event: Top track draws, headed THE FOLLOWER MODEL: post → a closed GATE marked 'build an audience first' → reach
A post arrives at the gate and STOPS there, held shut — the track visibly does not complete
Bottom track draws, headed THE INTEREST MODEL: post → match → reach, with no gate in the line
A post crosses straight through the match node and lands in reach
The match node fills TERRACOTTA and its label sets: 'matches what they already care about' — the accent marks the thing that replaced the gate

data.slideMeta: What a post has to get past
data.oldFoot: reach was rented from an audience you had to build
newSteps: matches what they already care about
data.newFoot: reach is earned by the post, not by the account
data.note: The gate did not get easier. It stopped being the gate.

beats.narration_text: So the real question changed too. It isn't how do I get more followers. It's how do I make something that earns attention on its own — one post at a time.

show.event: The old job card sets on the left: 'How do I get more followers?' with a RETIRED band
The card desaturates and settles back — retired, not deleted, and never faded past the legibility floor
The new job card rises on the right in TERRACOTTA: 'How do I make something that earns attention on its own?'
Beneath it a row of small post marks ticks on one at a time as 'one post at a time' lands — unlabelled marks, no count shown
Closer sets under the pair

data.slideMeta: The question a marketer is actually answering
data.oldQuestion: How do I get more followers?
data.newQuestion: How do I make something that earns attention on its own?
data.note: Followers used to be the strategy. Now they are the residue of it.

beats.narration_text: Worth being exact. This isn't that followers are worthless — they stopped being the entry fee. And this is one person's read, paraphrased from Gary Vaynerchuk, not a study. Test it on your own feed.

show.event: Left ledger heads WHAT THIS CLAIMS and three lines stack in under it
Right ledger heads WHAT IT DOESN'T and its lines stack in TERRACOTTA — the accent sits on the refusals, where the honesty is
A muted provenance rule draws across the foot, crediting Gary Vaynerchuk and naming this a paraphrase, not a study
The falsifier lands last: 'Test it on your own feed.'

data.title: What this is, and isn't

claims.heading: What this claims
items: feeds sort by interest signals, not only by follows
a post can travel before an audience exists
the job shifted from building reach to earning it

refusals.heading: What it doesn't
items: that followers are worthless — they stopped being the entry fee
that every feed works the same way
that this is measured — no figures are claimed here

data.provenance: Framing credited to Gary Vaynerchuk — paraphrased throughout, not quoted, and not a study.
data.falsifier: Test it on your own feed.

beats.narration_text: So — the shift. Social media became interest media. The feed sorts by what you watch, not who you follow. Followers stopped being the gate. The job is earning attention, one post at a time. And that's changing how Yatra thinks about content for Humanitarians AI.

show.event: Claude artifact page opens
Line one lands — the rename, credited
Line two lands — the sort key
Line three lands — the gate that stopped being a gate
Line four lands — the job
Line five lands and holds — what it changes for Humanitarians AI

artifactLines: The rename: social media became interest media. Framing credited to Gary Vaynerchuk — paraphrased here, not quoted.
The sort key: your feed is ordered by what you watch, pause on and search for — not by who you follow.
The gate: followers used to be the entry fee for reach. A post can now travel before an audience exists.
The job: make something that earns attention on its own — one post at a time.
Why it matters here: this is changing how Yatra thinks about content for Humanitarians AI.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Scroll your own feed, then paste this: look at the last twenty things my feed showed me — how many came from accounts I actually follow, and what interest were the rest matching? Look for whether it names the interest.

show.event: Serif 'Your turn.' replaces the persona greeting
The prompt types itself in as the narration reads it aloud, verbatim
Terracotta send arms
Three-item rubric stacks in as each check is discussed

props.command: Look at the last twenty things my feed showed me. How many came from accounts I actually follow, and what interest was each of the others matching? Then tell me which interest of mine the feed is most confident about.
output: grade it: can it name the interest, not just the account?
grade it: does it separate follows from matches?
grade it: does it say what it can't know from a feed alone?

beats.narration_text: Interest media. Not social media. This is Bella, in for Yatra — thanks for watching.
